title: Budget and Revenue
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

title: Budget and Revenue
text:
Budget and revenue
Figure 1 shows the relationship between film budgets and worldwide revenue. Each point represents one film in the dataset.

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (millions of US dollars)")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film budget against worldwide revenue

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
Runtime and rating
Figure 1 shows the relationship between a film’s runtime and its IMDb rating. Each point represents one film in the dataset.

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Film runtime against IMDb rating

title: Runtime and Ratings

films["decade"] = films["year"] // 10 * 10

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]

title: The Bond Films
text:
Bond revenue over time
The Bond films in this dataset range from 1995 to 2021.

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Worldwide revenue (millions of US dollars)")
plt.show()
